title: AsrElementV2
description: One raw ASR element inside a speaker monologue.

kind.description: Stable element kind selected by the worker adapter.

timing.description: When the element happened, or why that is not known.

AsrElementKindV2.description: Stable vocabulary for one monologue element returned by an ASR provider.

oneOf.description: Lexical content that should become transcript tokens.

AsrElementTimingV2.description:
When one ASR element happened, admitted once where the provider's numbers
were read: on the wire `{"kind": "timed", "start_ms", "end_ms"}` or
`{"kind": "untimed", "cause"}`.

One policy for every ASR route: a pair of bounds that is not an admissible
interval (inverted, or past the admissible range, as an epoch timestamp
would be) refuses the response the element came in, naming the element, as
the provider bridges refuse it; an absent bound is the provider's own
report and makes the element untimed with that cause.

oneOf.description: The provider timed the element, and the interval was admitted.

end_ms.description: The end, in milliseconds; never before the start.

start_ms.description: The start, in milliseconds from the start of the media.

oneOf.description: The element has no interval, for this reason.

UntimedCause.description:
Why an ASR word or element carries no interval.

A closed set, because "untimed" with no reason is how a fabricated zero got
in: once the reason has to be named, there is nowhere to hide a default.

oneOf.description: The provider reported an end but no start.
The provider reported a start but no end.

The enclosing segment carried no start, so the word's offsets cannot be
made absolute. Tencent's `StartMs` is the field in question; before this
state existed, an absent one became the start of the recording.
The provider reported a zero-width span, which locates nothing.

The bounds were present but not admissible (inverted, or past
[`AdmittedInterval::MAX_MS`]). The refusal itself is logged where the
bounds were read; the word carries no time and says so.
